text_blocks.snippet: In Arkansas, joint custody is generally favored in child custody cases, meaning both parents share responsibility for the child's upbringing. However, courts will still make decisions based on the child's best interests, and may order sole custody if it's deemed necessary.
snippet_highlighted_words: joint custody is generally favored in child custody cases, meaning both parents share responsibility for the child's upbringing

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of Arkansas custody law:

list.title: Joint Custody as the Default:
list.snippet: Arkansas law presumes that joint custody is in the child's best interest, meaning both parents share in making decisions and have significant time with the child.

list.title: Rebuttable Presumption:
list.snippet: This presumption can be overcome if one parent proves, with clear and convincing evidence, that joint custody is not in the child's best interest.
